current_notes: Before anything else, the one idea everything rests on: the cut-off lambda. For every held-out row, we measure how wrong the critic is: the gap between the target and the critic's value, scaled by BCA's learned unit. A rule reads a sample of these rows, which we call a bank, and picks one cut-off, lambda. Its promise is that at most 10 percent of new rows will be worse than that. Lambda times sigma is the safety band around the critic, and the width of that band becomes the dose. If lambda is too low, the band is too narrow and the actor trusts the critic where it's wrong. That's a failure. If it's too high, we're just more careful than we need to be. Because a sample's own 90 percent point lands too low about half the time, every rule adds a margin.

text: THE KEY IDEA · SUCCESS VS FAILURE
When does λ succeed, and when does it fail?
Valid if at most 5% of banks fail
A row is covered if its score is at most λ: the critic's error fits inside the band. Above λ, it is missed.

λ's miss rate is the share of all fresh rows in the frozen pool that score above it. The pool is frozen, so this number is exact.
Above 10%, the bank fails.

Each rule runs on 1,000 to 10,000 banks. It is valid if at most 1 bank in 20 fails (β = 0.95).
A rule that abstains (λ = ∞) makes no claim, so that bank counts as a pass.
HOW TO READ EVERY RESULT IN THIS DECK
Each number is the share of banks that fail, set against the 5% line. WBCP fails 4.9%: valid. RCPS fails 1.5%: valid, but cautious. W-CRC fails 49%: not valid.
Source  The “at least 95% of banks” standard is a high-probability guarantee, as in Bates et al. (2021).
current_notes: So how do we decide if lambda worked? Three levels. A row is covered if its score is under lambda, missed if it's over. A bank fails if lambda misses more than 10 percent of all the fresh rows in the pool, and because the pool is frozen, that's exact, not estimated. And a rule is valid if at most 1 bank in 20 fails. Every number in the rest of the talk is that last one: the share of banks that fail, compared with 5 percent.

current_notes: Every test works the same way. We train a critic, freeze it, and score a big pile of held-out data. Because the pile never changes, we know the exact right answer. Then we draw thousands of random samples, which we call banks. A method draws its safety line from each one, and we count how often that line is wrong. A bank fails if its line is wrong more than 1 time in 10. A method passes if at most 1 bank in 20 fails. Think of it as checking a thermometer against a known temperature thousands of times. text: WBCP: the cut-off 95% of reweighted banks agree on

We made 1,000 slightly different versions of the same bank by randomly changing how much each row counts. Each light line is one version (25 shown). It climbs as the cut-off moves right and more rows fall under it.
A line shows the share of rows below each cut-off. Where it crosses 90% is that version's cut-off (dot). Dots spread because a bank is only a sample.

current_notes: Here's how WBCP picks the line. It imagines many slightly different versions of the sample; each light curve is one. Each version would pick its own cut-off, shown as the dots. WBCP takes the cut-off that 95 percent of them agree on, and that's where '95 percent sure' comes from. With equal weights, this is exactly what BCA uses today. With importance weights, it can handle shift.

text: The task: hold five floats at rest against the water
WHY THIS WORLD  every value is exact, by simulation

current_notes: Five floats sit in a row in a channel, tied together by weak springs. A steady current and waves push every float downstream. Four thrusters sit between neighbouring floats: thruster 1 pushes floats 1 and 2, thruster 2 pushes floats 2 and 3, and so on. The controller holds the floats at rest while spending little throttle. The twist: past 80% throttle the propeller stalls and the push falls (0.65 at 90%, 0.5 at full throttle, against 0.8 at 80%), while the throttle still costs energy. Width U = λ × σ(s, a) at each logged row; u = the residual unit. In the code, safe_u is U and safe_c is u (rescaled as u_norm, c_norm).
